## Natural history notes

A native sunfish characterized by its deep, stocky body, large mouth, dark mottled coloration, and reddish eyes. In Florida, it is found in slow-moving freshwater habitats such as swamps, marshes, ponds, lakes, canals, and vegetated streams. It feeds on insects, crayfish, small fish, and other aquatic animals, often using dense vegetation, roots, logs, and other cover for ambush and shelter.
